newsitem.title: USA: U.S. FERC asserts say over Green Canyon Gathering.
newsitem.headline: U.S. FERC asserts say over Green Canyon Gathering.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission on Wednesday asserted authority over rates to be charged on Green Canyon Gathering Co's proposed natural gas pipeline in the Gulf of Mexico.

The commission denied a request by the company to treat the pipeline as a gathering line which is outside the commission's authority, saying that because the pipeline was to be in shallow water only, it was within its jurisdiction.
The commission also reaffirmed a ruling from last year that it had jurisdiction over Shell Gas Pipeline Co's Garden Banks Gathering System.
Shell Gas Pipeline Co is a subsidiary of Shell Oil.
Green Canyon Gathering is a subsidiary of Tennessee Gas Pipeline Co which is owned by El Paso Energy.

Green Canyon plans to build 133 miles of pipeline from the Louisiana coast into water about 192 meters deep, where the system will be able to connect with pipelines from the Green Canyon, Ewing Bank and Mississippi Canyon deepwater areas.
Outer continental shelf areas where the commission has opted for less regulation are considered to be depths of at least 200 meters.

Producers who do not own pipelines want the commission to excercise jurisdiction over the offshore pipelines to ensure that those who have few options for shipping their production onshore are not subject to unfair rates.
